canonical.title: Detect Cycle in an Undirected Graph
canonical.sourceFilePath: 13. Graphs/2. Traversal Problems/04. Detect Cycle in Undirected Graph.cpp

narrative.title: The Redundant Duct Audit
narrative.scenario: A plant's air-duct network is undirected, and the auditor must flag whether any duct forms a loop — a ring that lets air return to where it started without retracing. Walking the network from junction to junction, the only legitimate way to meet an already-logged junction is the one you just came from; meeting any other logged junction means a loop exists.
narrative.inputFormat: An integer V and an adjacency list adj where adj[i] lists every junction directly connected to junction i.
narrative.outputFormat: Return true if the undirected graph contains a cycle, otherwise false.

testCases.explanation: 0-1-2-0 closes a triangle; junction 3 is an innocent bystander.
The square 0-1-3-2-0 is a four-way loop.

hintLevels: Level 1: In an undirected walk, every edge back to where you just were is expected — anything else visited is a loop.
Level 2: Recurse with the parent id; treat the parent as the only legal already-visited neighbour.
Level 3: Run the sweep per component: an unvisited node at top level opens a fresh DFS with parent -1.
